title: The First Letter of John and the Johannine Letters
lead: The three letters of John are among the shortest books of the New Testament, and the first of them is one of the most loved. 1 John has no greeting or name; 2 and 3 John come from "the Elder". All three share the language of John's Gospel: truth, love, remaining, the command "from the beginning". 1 John answers a split: some members had left, and the letter calls the one who denies that Jesus is the Messiah an antichrist; 2 John warns a church about such teachers; 3 John deals with a leader who refused hospitality to the Elder's messengers. This page is about the letters; for the people named John, see the person page.

sections.b: Most scholars think one writer stands behind all three letters, though there is no consensus on whether he also wrote the Gospel, or who he was: the apostle John (the traditional view), John the Elder known to Papias, or another teacher of John's circle. 1 John reads like a written sermon for several churches; 2 John is a short letter to "the chosen lady and her children", a church or a household; 3 John is a private note to Gaius. In the early church the first letter was accepted everywhere, while the second and third were for a time among the disputed books (Eusebius, Church History 3.25.2-3).
